notes: Score the exercises a learner would get, not how much method the reply describes. A set fails outright if any item gives its answer's code or steps in the prompt, if a solution does not answer its item, if a command, flag or API was neither run nor checked against current docs, if an item asks only for a fact, or if a readiness set contains anything from the repository or was written into it. A set also fails if it skipped the coverage check without saying so, if any item carries a hint or a check sentence, if any item installs the tool, if the README has prose between the title and the list, or if an item makes the learner read or write material from outside the target that a one-line stand-in could replace. A review fails if it rewrites items that were already fine, or renumbers or changes the meaning of an item that has an Exercise N commit. Score each output against a run without the skill: a set that does not beat that baseline on these points is not finished.

evals.prompt: I want to learn DuckDB properly. Write the activities for it.
evals.expected_output: A duckdb-activities README in the activities format, built on one dataset, ordered so each idea is introduced, reused and mixed, with every command checked against the current DuckDB docs.
assertions: The README is the title `# DuckDB Activities` followed directly by the numbered list, with no description or version line
No item installs DuckDB, and item 1 ends with a visible result
Every item is one or two short sentences, with no `Check:` sentence and almost no inline code
No item contains the SQL or commands that answer it; those appear only inside `<details>` blocks
The set includes at least one predict item, one break or fix item, one inspect item, and one compare or choose item
At least one later item uses an earlier feature without naming it
There is at least one review item, and the set ends with a capstone, then a recall item or a proposal for Anki review notes
It searched the Anki collection and the existing activity sets before writing, and the reply says what it skipped or sent to flashcards, and why
No item asks the learner only to state a fact
Every `<details>` block is indented to its item's text, with a blank line after `</summary>`, and is labelled `Solution`; no item has a hint
The reply says which solutions were run and which were only checked against the docs, and names the DuckDB version and date

evals.prompt: Turn the Terraform Get Started tutorial for AWS into exercises for me.
evals.expected_output: Short items that state outcomes rather than the tutorial's steps, with a prediction the plan settles and a teardown item, linking the tutorial in Resources.
assertions: No item tells the learner to copy or paste code from the tutorial
Items state outcomes, such as an instance that exists, not the tutorial's steps
At least one item asks for a prediction that `terraform plan` then settles
A teardown item comes last
A Resources list links the tutorial

evals.prompt: Add five more exercises to my dlt-activities.
evals.expected_output: Items 16 to 20 appended, reusing the set's Pokémon and GitHub pipelines, with the existing items untouched and the README change offered as a fixup commit.
assertions: It reads the existing README and git log before writing
The new items are numbered 16 to 20, and items 1 to 15 are unchanged
The new items build on the set's existing pipelines and names
At least one new item uses an earlier feature, such as a transformer or pagination, without naming it
Every new item is one or two short sentences, with no check
If it commits, the subject is `fixup! Set up the playground`, and it does not rebase or push without asking

evals.prompt: fastapi-activities has 13 Exercise commits but the README still says TODO. Write the statements.
evals.expected_output: Thirteen items written from the commits' diffs, numbered to match, each stating in a sentence the outcome its diff achieves.
assertions: It reads each Exercise commit's diff before writing its item
It writes 13 items, numbered 1 to 13 to match the commits
Each item states the outcome its diff achieves, not a description of the diff
Each item is one or two short sentences, with no check
It changes no commit, and flags any commit whose purpose it cannot tell

evals.prompt: Review my weft-activities README.
evals.expected_output: A per-item review that keeps item 1, and reports that item 2's statement asks for a package name its Exercise 2 commit computes instead.
assertions: It reads the README and the Exercise commits
It keeps item 1's statement word for word
It reports that item 2 asks the user for a package name while the commit computes it
It asks which of the two is right instead of silently changing either
It does not renumber anything

evals.prompt: Write the reference solution for exercise 4 of my activities and commit it.
evals.expected_output: One commit named exactly `Exercise 4`, holding only that exercise's files, with the solution run before committing.
assertions: The commit subject is exactly `Exercise 4`, with no body or prefix
The commit holds only that exercise's files, and not the README
The solution was run before committing
Commands the commit cannot show go in the item's Solution block, as a separate `fixup! Set up the playground` commit

evals.prompt: Write exercises so my colleague can learn dbt. She knows SQL well but has never used git.
evals.expected_output: A dbt set that skips SQL basics, keeps git out of the items since git is not what the set teaches, and spends every item on dbt.
assertions: No item teaches SQL basics or git
Git commands the set needs appear in the setup commit or inside solutions, never as items of their own
dbt features are named on first use and not named on later uses
No item installs dbt, and no item has a check sentence

evals.prompt: Write a learning set for Kestra.
evals.expected_output: A set built from the current Kestra docs, with the version pinned, and no command, flag or API that was not read in the docs or run.
assertions: It reads the current Kestra documentation before writing any item
The reply names the Kestra version and date the set was checked against, and the README does not
Every command, flag and API in the set appears in the docs it read, or was run
It does not ask the user anything the docs answer

evals.prompt: Make Anki cards from the dlt docs.

It routes to anki-flashcards

evals.prompt: Write a getting-started tutorial for our CLI's documentation site.

assertions: It does not write exercises or an activities README
It routes to writing-documentation

evals.prompt: Explain how Kafka consumer groups rebalance.

assertions: It does not write a README unasked
If it mentions this skill, it says live quizzing is out of scope and offers predict or recall items as the alternative

It does not produce an activities README with hidden solutions for candidates

evals.prompt: Write the activities for Polars and commit them.
evals.expected_output: With writing-commits and humanizer loaded alongside: the README is committed as `Set up the playground`, and its prose has no generated tics.
assertions: The commit subject is `Set up the playground`, not a subject rewritten to writing-commits' style
No item uses an em dash as glue, a synonym triad, or the words "just", "simply" or "easy"
The rules of the set itself still hold: short outcomes and hidden solutions, with no checks or hints

evals.prompt: I start on this Rust repository next week. Write exercises that check I master the Rust features it uses.
evals.expected_output: A readiness part for the learner's rust-activities, built from an inventory of the features the repository's code uses, with generic real-world exercises and nothing from the repository.
assertions: It reads the workspace manifests and counts the features the code uses before choosing exercises
The reply shows the inventory with a decision per feature, including features skipped as barely used or already carded
No item contains code, file names, identifiers, domain terms or data from the repository
Every item is a realistic task on a neutral project of its own, and some items combine several features
The set goes into the learner's rust-activities, in a part named after the features, and nothing is written into the repository
Basics the collection already cards, such as formatting with `println!`, get no exercise

evals.prompt: Write exercises for printing and formatting in Rust.
evals.expected_output: The carded formatting syntax gets nothing, uncarded syntax rules go to flashcards, and exercises cover only the practice neither the cards nor the existing sets cover, as realistic tasks.
assertions: It searches the collection and finds the existing formatting cards
It writes no exercise that only recalls formatting syntax, and lists uncarded syntax rules for flashcards instead
Every item it writes is a realistic task, such as a report or a table to print, that needs the formatting practice it covers
The reply says, concept by concept, what was skipped and why

evals.prompt: Write exercises so I learn the CAP theorem.

assertions: It does not write an activities README of questions about the theorem

If it proposes any exercise, the exercise is a hands-on task, such as observing a partition with a real database

evals.prompt: Write more dbt exercises for me.
evals.expected_output: Only the gaps: the collection holds many dbt cards and dbt-activities already has done exercises, so the new items cover practice found in neither.
assertions: It reads the existing dbt-activities README and its Exercise N commits
It searches the collection under the dbt context field
No new item repeats an exercise the learner has done
The reply lists what it skipped and where each skipped concept is already covered

The exercises target the TypeScript, framework and library versions the repository pins
